status: design-input; Stage-0 implementations must reproduce this contract exactly

query_clock.event_effective: event.valid_from <= cut.valid_time AND (event.valid_to_or_null == null OR cut.valid_time < event.valid_to_or_null)
query_clock.currentness: reduce only events for which event_visible AND event_effective are true, in ascending journal_seq
query_clock.ties: journal_seq is the sole total-order tie breaker; event_id never breaks time ties
query_clock.retroactivity: fact assertion/correction/retraction events may have valid_from < observed_at; all obligation, dependency, and handoff events require valid_from == observed_at and valid_to_or_null == null
query_clock.prior_cut_rule: an event observed after a prior cut never changes that prior cut, even when its valid_from is retroactive

global_guards: journal_seq is a positive contiguous integer assigned only by the single writer
idempotency_key is unique per scope_id and semantic operation
valid_to_or_null is null or strictly greater than valid_from
all referenced event, subject, obligation, action, dependency, and handoff IDs exist unless the event type explicitly creates that ID
every source_event_id is less than the new journal_seq
duplicate event_id or duplicate idempotency_key returns DUPLICATE_NOOP and appends no second semantic effect

state.fact_current_rule: for each fact_key, choose the greatest-journal_seq visible, effective, unretracted version in the one linear supersession chain; if that version is retracted or out of interval, walk parent_event_id_or_null until an eligible ancestor is found; otherwise the key has no current value

derived_sets.O_blocked: lifecycle == OPEN AND at least one prerequisite lifecycle != COMPLETED
derived_sets.O_due: lifecycle == OPEN AND due_at <= cut.valid_time AND obligation not in O_blocked

state.scope_rule: scope_id is immutable for facts, obligations, dependencies, and handoffs; delegation changes owner_role only; cross-scope delegation and cross-scope dependency edges are illegal

guards: no fact chain exists for fact_key
supersedes_event_id_or_null names the current visible fact_version for the same fact_key at (journal_seq-1, observed_at, valid_from)
the new edge cannot create a cycle or sibling branch
correct_fact.effect: create child fact_version whose parent_event_id is supersedes_event_id_or_null; prior versions remain available outside the child validity interval or after legal retraction

guards: supersedes_event_id_or_null names the current visible fact_version for the same fact_key at (journal_seq-1, observed_at, valid_from)
the target has no earlier visible effective retraction
retract_fact.effect: mark the named version retracted during this event validity interval; fact_current_rule restores the nearest eligible ancestor or no value

guards: due_at is an RFC3339 UTC instant
open_obligation.effect: create obligation with lifecycle OPEN and empty prerequisite_obligation_ids

guards: obligation exists in the same scope
obligation exists in the same scope
new_owner_role is in the frozen role catalog
obligation exists in the same scope
obligation is in O_due at the event cut
complete_obligation.effect: set lifecycle COMPLETED and terminal_event_id to this event_id

guards: obligation exists in the same scope
reason_code is in the frozen cancellation-code catalog
cancel_obligation.effect: set lifecycle CANCELLED and terminal_event_id to this event_id

guards: obligation exists in the same scope
new_due_at is an RFC3339 UTC instant
reopen_obligation.effect: set lifecycle OPEN, due_at new_due_at, owner_role payload.owner_role, terminal_event_id null; retain prerequisite set

guards: both obligations exist and are OPEN in event.scope_id
adding edge leaves the directed graph acyclic
target obligation exists, is OPEN, and is in event.scope_id
no other OPEN, RESPONSE_RECORDED, or PROPOSED handoff targets the same obligation
response_ref identifies immutable raw response bytes
record_handoff_response.effect: set handoff status RESPONSE_RECORDED and recorded_response_event_id to this event_id; parse, validation, commit, rejection, and recovery must read these recorded bytes and may not resample the accepted request

guards: worker_handoff_v1 is schema-valid, scope-valid, hash-bound to the input packet, and within every cap
propose_handoff_result.effect: set handoff status PROPOSED and proposal_event_id to this event_id

guards: every committed action is available and legal at this event cut
proposal idempotency key has no committed effect
commit_handoff_result.effect: apply each validated action once through ordinary event transitions; set handoff status COMMITTED and terminal_event_id to this event_id

guards: handoff status is RESPONSE_RECORDED or PROPOSED
rejection_code is one of SCHEMA_INVALID, WRONG_SCOPE, STALE_INPUT, ACTION_UNAVAILABLE, ILLEGAL_TRANSITION, HASH_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE
reject_handoff_result.effect: append no proposed semantic mutation; set handoff status REJECTED and terminal_event_id to this event_id

guards: handoff status is COMMITTED or REJECTED
close_handoff.effect: set handoff status CLOSED; preserve terminal_event_id of commit or rejection

illegal_transition_result.append_policy: the attempted event is retained in the runner audit log but is not appended to the canonical journal

catalog.precondition: the obligation has any visible lifecycle event in the scenario world

action_universe.deterministic_core_constraint: each scored scenario has 7 through 15 obligation IDs total across mounted and unmounted scopes, so the complete enumerated list including NO_ACTION has 8 through 16 IDs
action_universe.available_action_ids: UTF8-bytewise sort of NO_ACTION plus ACT:{scope_id}:{obligation_id} for every obligation with any visible lifecycle event at the cut; no generator-supplied ad hoc action ID is legal
action_universe.gold_action_ids: UTF8-bytewise sort of ACT IDs for every critical obligation in O_due whose scope is mounted; if this set is empty, gold is [NO_ACTION]; otherwise NO_ACTION is not gold
action_universe.gold_cardinality: one through four ACT IDs, or the singleton NO_ACTION
action_universe.frontier_axis_rule: F=64 and F=256 cells are deterministic resource cells, not paid/action-scored cells, and may exceed the 8-through-16 action envelope

paid_handoff_gold.cut_selection: among cuts with at least one mounted critical O_due obligation and at least one non-gold available action, choose the cut with the smallest SHA256 of scenario_id + '|' + cut_id + '|stage2-cut-v1'
paid_handoff_gold.A0_target: the UTF8-bytewise smallest gold ACT ID at the selected cut
paid_handoff_gold.A1_gold: recompute gold_action_ids after the deterministic writer commits B's valid completion; the committed target action must not appear again
paid_handoff_gold.contract_success: 1 iff A0 selects exactly A0_target and emits a schema-valid task, B proposes exactly one legal completion for B_target with no extra mutation, the writer commits exactly one effect, and cold A1 emits exactly A1_gold with no stale, terminal, premature, or wrong-scope action; otherwise 0

serialization.time_format: RFC3339 UTC with exactly six fractional digits and suffix Z
serialization.array_order: semantic ID UTF8-bytewise ascending unless this contract specifies journal_seq order
serialization.numbers: integers only in the state/action contract; no NaN, infinity, or negative zero

mandatory_enumerator_checks: all 17 event types have at least one legal and one illegal fixture
every ordered two-event type pair is either witnessed as legal or returns a named illegal-transition code
correction cycles and dependency cycles are rejected
correct then retract restores the nearest eligible ancestor
retroactive correction changes a later knowledge cut but never rewrites a prior cut
four simultaneous due critical obligations yield four gold ACT IDs
wrong-scope same-name obligations remain available distractors but never gold
raw accepted response is replayed after crash without a second provider request
duplicate proposal and duplicate commit produce one committed effect
